contract_verdicts.evidence: backend/src/mapping/mis-mapping-master.ts:7 declares the versioned master as a COMPILED TS const (not a runtime-parsed JSON file, so it survives `node dist/main.js`) with selection records keyed by department+function+canonical plant owning the aliases and mis_format; backend/src/mapping/mapping-master.ts:75 is the strict loader that rejects a malformed master, a duplicate selection key, a duplicate (cost_centre, gl) entry, an alias reused across selections and a reason-less provisional entry.

backend/src/mapping/mis-mapping-master.ts:60 gives the nine unresolved DUB triples EXPLICIT unmapped-GL entries, each provisional with a reason; backend/src/mapping/mapping-master.db.test.ts:23 is the gated D-0008 proof that every ingested DUB triple resolves exactly once - 66 mapped + 22 bucketed = 88 rows, no fan-out. Re-run on the merged tree here: test:warehouse-proof 16/16.

backend/src/ingest/plant-mapping.ts:1 now derives canonicalPlant() from the master instead of a hard-coded alias table, so the master is the single alias authority; the three pre-existing gated warehouse tests and July's DUB reconciliation total are unchanged, which is the proof the derivation is faithful.

backend/src/mapping/selection-resolver.service.ts:59 resolves a selection through the master and backend/src/mis/mis-selection.service.ts:67 returns the resolved/unresolvable union; STORY ACCEPTANCE 3 rides on this - an unknown plant yields the unresolvable outcome rather than a 403, a split the selection-resolution review round forced.

backend/src/sql/sqlBuilder.ts:144 filters the Actual side by the master's resolved triples BEFORE the (gl_code, month) roll-up - decision 0017's 'filter before the rollup, one governed path' - and backend/src/warehouse/selection-slice.db.test.ts:21 proves one exact row per GL and month with no fan-out against really-ingested data.

backend/src/mis/mis-selection.controller.ts:27 exposes GET /api/mis/options and POST /api/mis/run behind the governed grants, registered at backend/src/app.module.ts:11, following the vendored house style per decision 0019; both routes were exercised live (200) during the selection-ui functional check.

frontend/src/features/mis/mis-report-view.tsx:41 renders the four native selects populated from the options route and posts exactly the four selectors through frontend/src/lib/api.ts:61. Proven live on the merged stack: Agriculture/Nursery/DUB/2026-07-01 returned the DUB nursery slice - 28 GL rows, Actual Rs 1,15,12,712.07 - which is STORY ACCEPTANCE 1.

frontend/src/features/mis/mis-report-view.tsx:135 branches on the response UNION rather than row emptiness, so a configured zero result and an unresolvable selection are distinct on screen; frontend/src/features/mis/mis-report-view.test.tsx:83 proves both, which is STORY ACCEPTANCE 3 (zeros plus the 'no mapping configured' notice, no crash).

frontend/src/features/mis/mis-report-view.tsx:217 renders the unmapped-GL bucket as a reviewable list - one row per GL after the review-driven fold, each carrying an Actual and a Budget amount, its cost centres named explicitly via costCentres, and its reason - and frontend/src/components/shell/app-shell.tsx:11 enables the MIS Reports nav item. Verified live: 9 bucket rows with reasons.

summary: No performance regression across the story. Decision 0017's ruling - filter before the roll-up, one governed path - is honoured in sqlBuilder.ts:144: the master's resolved triples narrow the Actual side BEFORE aggregation and the period predicate is pushed into both source CTEs, so neither side aggregates rows it will discard, and no second query path was forked. The autoreview round that demanded per-triple bucket amounts was answered by folding the bucket display to GL grain rather than adding a warehouse query path, so the page still issues exactly two requests - one options call and one run call - and the builder and executor were left untouched. The aggregate gated proof runs 16/16 in ~19s serialized; the dead-port control fails 6 leaves with ECONNREFUSED, so the timing is real work, not skips.
